name: notion-contact-to-newsletter-subscriber

trigger.trigger_note: Catch hook, posted to by a button property on the Notion Contacts data source. `webhook_url` is the one external systems call; `trigger_url` is Zapier-internal and must never be handed out. THIS IS A NEW URL — the Notion button must be repointed at it or this Zap never fires (see `cutover`). Notion button properties deliver an EMPTY body every time someone tests them while wiring up, which is precisely why the empty-payload guard matters here.

connection_notes.notion_wf: work.flowers | Dennis <dennis@work.flowers>. NEVER the `Knoxx | Dennis #2` connection (02b95b31-c152-8800-9036-1107e08f70da), which cannot see work.flowers databases.

notion.note: The contact page is re-read with sdk.fetch against the Notion REST API rather than trusted from the webhook payload — the address may have been edited in the same breath as the click. Nothing is written to Notion; the `Mailing List` tick comes back round via new-buttondown-subscriber-update-in-notion once Buttondown confirms.

buttondown.action: ButtondownCLIAPI write subscriber, with automatically_activate: true
buttondown.firewall_finding: Buttondown answers a re-subscribe of an existing address with `This subscriber was blocked by your firewall` (partner_error, HTTP 200) — NOT an 'already exists' message, and indistinguishable from a genuine firewall refusal of a brand-new address. Reproduced live on 2026-08-10 (run 019febef-133f-7f63-b9a7-37864a9c51eb), where it burned all five step retries and failed the run. The workflow therefore looks before it writes: `search subscriber` first (a miss returns `{data: []}`, not an error), short-circuit if found, and only then create. Any refusal that survives that check is real and fails loudly, by design — a lead silently not subscribed is worse than an alert.

behaviour_changes_vs_classic_zap: Empty-payload guard (repo rule). A Notion button property delivers an empty body on every test click during setup; that now returns {skipped: "empty-payload"} instead of raising. A payload with content but no usable page id still throws.
Re-reads the contact page instead of trusting the webhook snapshot.
Skips (does not raise) when Primary Email is empty — the classic Zap's `Primary Email Populated` filter, which halted silently.
Skips when the contact page is archived or in the trash.
Idempotent on a repeated click: the pre-check finds the existing subscriber and short-circuits.

cutover.status: PENDING — Dennis to repoint the Notion Contacts button property at the webhook_url above, then disable the classic Zap.
cutover.why_it_matters: Until the button is repointed this durable has an active trigger and zero traffic, while the classic Zap keeps serving. Each button posts to exactly one URL, so there is no double-fire window.
cutover.not_machine_verifiable: Classic Zaps are exposed by neither the SDK CLI nor the MCP connector, so the disable must be done and confirmed in the Zapier UI.

Chosen so the run exercised page fetch, email extraction and the subscriber pre-check end to end without creating a subscriber.
